cls: Local anaesthetic (active in acid), with antacids
pharm: Local anaesthetic (active in acid), with antacids
quick: 10 to 20 mg oxetacaine (typically 5 to 10 mL of a 10 mg/5 mL antacid gel) three to four times daily
Dizziness, drowsiness, Nausea, constipation or diarrhoea (antacid)
summary: Oxetacaine (oxethazaine) is a potent local anaesthetic that stays un-ionised and active at gastric pH. It is combined with aluminium and magnesium hydroxide in antacid gels to relieve the pain of gastritis, oesophagitis and peptic ulcer.
indications: Symptomatic relief of pain in gastritis, reflux oesophagitis, peptic ulcer and hiatus hernia, with antacids

dosage.d: 10 to 20 mg oxetacaine (typically 5 to 10 mL of a 10 mg/5 mL antacid gel) three to four times daily
dosage.n: 15 minutes before meals and at bedtime

admin: Shake well; take undiluted 15 minutes before meals
Do not exceed the labelled daily amount
moa: Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels in gastric mucosal nerve endings, producing topical anaesthesia of the mucosa; unlike most local anaesthetics it remains active in acid.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to oxetacaine or amide local anaesthetics
relative: Severe renal impairment (magnesium and aluminium in the combination)

renal: Avoid prolonged use of the antacid combination in severe renal impairment (magnesium and aluminium accumulation)

moderate: The antacid component reduces absorption of tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, iron, levothyroxine and digoxin: separate by 2 to 4 hours

counsel: May cause drowsiness or dizziness; do not drive if affected
Do not use for more than a few days without review
pearls: Masks ulcer pain: investigate persistent dyspepsia rather than extending use
missed: Take it when remembered unless the next dose is due; do not double up.
overdose: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity is possible: supportive care, treat seizures with benzodiazepines; lipid emulsion per local protocol.
